audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for parable discourse: sower, hearing/understanding, Isaiah citation, seed/soil, weeds, mustard, leaven, hidden treasure, pearl, net, householder, and Nazareth rejection.

verses.restored: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.

familiar.text: The same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.

modern.text: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the sea.

original.text: ⸀Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·

verses.restored: Great crowds gathered to him, so that he entered a boat and sat, and all the crowd stood on the shore.

familiar.text: And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship, and sat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore.

modern.text: Such large crowds gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore.

original.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν ⸀εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.

verses.restored: He spoke many things to them in parables, saying, Look, the sower went out to sow.

familiar.text: And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow;

modern.text: And He told them many things in parables, saying, “A farmer went out to sow his seed.

original.text: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.

verses.restored: As he sowed, some fell beside the way, and the birds came and devoured them.

familiar.text: And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up:

modern.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

original.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ⸂ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ⸃ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.

verses.restored: Other seed fell on rocky places where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil.

familiar.text: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth:

modern.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

original.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς,

verses.restored: When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.

familiar.text: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.

modern.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

original.text: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.

verses.restored: Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.

familiar.text: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:

modern.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.

original.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ⸀ἔπνιξαν αὐτά.

verses.restored: Other seed fell on beautiful/good soil and gave fruit: some hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

familiar.text: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

modern.text: Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop—a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.

original.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.

verses.restored: The one having ears, let him hear.

familiar.text: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.text: He who has ears, let him hear.” The Purpose of Jesus’ Parables (Isaiah 6:1–13; Mark 4:10–12; Luke 8:9–10)

original.text: ὁ ἔχων ⸀ὦτα ἀκουέτω.

verses.restored: The disciples came and said to him, Why do you speak to them in parables?

familiar.text: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?

modern.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why do You speak to the people in parables?”

original.text: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;

verses.restored: He answered, To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the reign of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.

familiar.text: He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.

modern.text: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Ὅτι ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.

verses.restored: For whoever has, more will be given and he will overflow; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.

familiar.text: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

modern.text: Whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

original.text: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Because of this I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear or understand.

familiar.text: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.

modern.text: This is why I speak to them in parables: ‘Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.’

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·

verses.restored: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: With hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.

familiar.text: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive:

modern.text: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: ‘You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.

original.text: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.

verses.restored: For this people's heart has grown thick; with their ears they hardly hear, and their eyes they have closed, lest they see with the eyes, hear with the ears, understand with the heart, turn back, and I heal them.

familiar.text: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

modern.text: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’

original.text: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.

verses.restored: But blessed/flourishing are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.

familiar.text: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.

modern.text: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.

original.text: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ⸀ἀκούουσιν.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: many prophets and righteous ones desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.

familiar.text: For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

modern.text: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it. The Parable of the Sower Explained (Mark 4:13–20; Luke 8:11–15)

original.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

verses.restored: You, then, hear the parable of the sower.

familiar.text: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.

modern.text: Consider, then, the parable of the sower:

original.text: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ ⸀σπείραντος.

verses.restored: When anyone hears the word of the reign and does not understand, the harmful one comes and seizes what was sown in his heart; this is what was sown beside the way.

familiar.text: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.

modern.text: When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.

original.text: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.

verses.restored: The one sown on rocky places is the one hearing the word and immediately receiving it with joy,

familiar.text: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;

modern.text: The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν,

verses.restored: yet he has no root in himself but is temporary; when pressure or persecution happens because of the word, immediately he stumbles.

familiar.text: Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.

modern.text: But since he has no root, he remains for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.

original.text: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.

verses.restored: The one sown among thorns is the one hearing the word, but the worry of the age and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.

familiar.text: He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.

modern.text: The seed sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος ⸀τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.

verses.restored: The one sown on beautiful/good soil is the one hearing the word and understanding it, who indeed bears fruit and produces: one hundredfold, one sixty, one thirty.

familiar.text: But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

modern.text: But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and produces a crop—a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.” The Parable of the Weeds (Ezekiel 17:1–10)

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ⸂καλὴν γῆν⸃ σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ⸀συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.

verses.restored: He set another parable before them, saying, The reign of the heavens is like a person sowing beautiful/good seed in his field.

familiar.text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:

modern.text: Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.

original.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ⸀σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: While people slept, his enemy came, sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away.

familiar.text: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.

modern.text: But while everyone was asleep, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.

original.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ⸀ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.

verses.restored: When the grass sprouted and made fruit, then the weeds appeared also.

familiar.text: But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.

modern.text: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.

verses.restored: The servants of the householder came and said, Lord, did you not sow beautiful/good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have weeds?

familiar.text: So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?

modern.text: The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’

original.text: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ⸀ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;

verses.restored: He said to them, An enemy person did this. The servants said, Then do you want us to go and gather them?

familiar.text: He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?

modern.text: ‘An enemy did this,’ he replied. So the servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and pull them up?’

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ ⸂δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν⸃· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες ⸀συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;

verses.restored: He said, No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat with them.

familiar.text: But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them.

modern.text: ‘No,’ he said, ‘if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.

original.text: ὁ δέ ⸀φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·

verses.restored: Let both grow together until the harvest; at harvest time I will say to the harvesters, Gather first the weeds and bind them into bundles to burn, but gather the wheat into my barn.

familiar.text: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.

modern.text: Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the harvesters: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.’” The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Mark 4:30–34; Luke 13:18–19)

original.text: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα ⸀μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον ⸀συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.

verses.restored: He set another parable before them, saying, The reign of the heavens is like a mustard seed, which a person took and sowed in his field.

familiar.text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:

modern.text: He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.

original.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: It is smaller than all seeds, but when grown it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the heavens come and nest in its branches.

familiar.text: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

modern.text: Although it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.” The Parable of the Leaven (Luke 13:20–21)

original.text: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He spoke another parable to them: The reign of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until it was all leavened.

familiar.text: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

modern.text: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.” I Will Open My Mouth in Parables (Psalms 78:1–72)

original.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ⸀ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.

verses.restored: All these things Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he spoke nothing to them,

familiar.text: All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:

modern.text: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.

original.text: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς ⸀οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·

verses.restored: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.

familiar.text: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.

modern.text: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.” The Parable of the Weeds Explained (Zephaniah 1:1–6)

original.text: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ ⸀καταβολῆς.

verses.restored: Then he left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.

familiar.text: Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.

modern.text: Then Jesus dismissed the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”

original.text: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ⸀οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· ⸀Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.

verses.restored: He answered, The one sowing the beautiful/good seed is the Son of Humanity.

familiar.text: He answered and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;

modern.text: He replied, “The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

verses.restored: The field is the world; the beautiful/good seed are the sons of the reign; the weeds are the sons of the harmful one.

familiar.text: The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;

modern.text: The field is the world, and the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one,

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,

verses.restored: The enemy who sowed them is the adversarial one; the harvest is the completion of the age, and the harvesters are messengers.

familiar.text: The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.

modern.text: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια ⸀αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.

verses.restored: Just as weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the completion of the age.

familiar.text: As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.

modern.text: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.

original.text: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ ⸀καίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ ⸀αἰῶνος·

verses.restored: The Son of Humanity will send his messengers, and they will gather out of his reign all stumbling-blocks and those doing lawlessness.

familiar.text: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;

modern.text: The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will weed out of His kingdom every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness.

original.text: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,

verses.restored: They will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

familiar.text: And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

modern.text: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

original.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

verses.restored: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the reign of their Father. The one having ears, let him hear.

familiar.text: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear. The Parables of the Treasure and the Pearl

original.text: Τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ⸀ὦτα ἀκουέτω.

verses.restored: The reign of the heavens is like treasure hidden in the field, which a person found and hid; in his joy he goes and sells all he has and buys that field.

familiar.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

modern.text: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.

original.text: ⸀Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ ⸂πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει⸃ καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.

verses.restored: Again, the reign of the heavens is like a merchant seeking beautiful pearls.

familiar.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:

modern.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.

original.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ⸀ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·

verses.restored: Finding one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it.

familiar.text: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

modern.text: When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it. The Parable of the Net

original.text: ⸂εὑρὼν δὲ⸃ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Again, the reign of the heavens is like a net cast into the sea and gathering from every kind.

familiar.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

modern.text: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish.

original.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·

verses.restored: When it was filled, they drew it onto the shore, sat down, gathered the good into containers, and threw out the rotten.

familiar.text: Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away.

modern.text: When it was full, the men pulled it ashore. Then they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away.

original.text: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ⸀ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.

verses.restored: So it will be at the completion of the age: the messengers will go out and separate the harmful from among the righteous.

familiar.text: So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,

modern.text: So will it be at the end of the age: The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous,

original.text: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων

verses.restored: They will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

familiar.text: And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

modern.text: and throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

original.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

verses.restored: Have you understood all these things? They said to him, Yes.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto them, Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.

modern.text: Have you understood all these things?” “Yes,” they answered.

original.text: ⸀Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· ⸀Ναί.

verses.restored: He said to them, Therefore every scribe discipled to the reign of the heavens is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.

familiar.text: Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

modern.text: Then He told them, “For this reason, every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.” The Rejection at Nazareth (Mark 6:1–6; Luke 4:16–30)

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς ⸂τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.

verses.restored: When Jesus finished these parables, he departed from there.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.

modern.text: When Jesus had finished these parables, He withdrew from that place.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.

verses.restored: Coming into his homeland, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, From where does this one have this wisdom and these powers?

familiar.text: And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?

modern.text: Coming to His hometown, He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were astonished. “Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?” they asked.

original.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;

verses.restored: Is this not the craftsman's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?

familiar.text: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?

modern.text: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?

original.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; ⸀οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;

verses.restored: And are not all his sisters with us? From where, then, does this one have all these things?

familiar.text: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

modern.text: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”

original.text: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;

verses.restored: They stumbled over him. But Jesus said to them, A prophet is not dishonored except in his homeland and in his house.

familiar.text: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.

modern.text: And they took offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

original.text: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ ⸀πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He did not do many powers there because of their lack of trust.

familiar.text: And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

modern.text: And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
